stops.title: LPP formulation & Graphical solution (Corner point method)
stops.inShort: A Linear Programming Problem maximizes or minimizes a linear objective function Z = ax + by subject to linear inequality constraints and non-negativity x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0. Optimal value always occurs at a corner point (vertex) of the bounded feasible region.

items.f: Optimize Z = a x + b y
items.s: Evaluate Z at every corner point of feasible region.

board.text: If the corner points of the feasible solution are (0, 10), (2, 2) and (4, 0) then the point of minimum Z = 3x + 2y is ____.
Maximize Z = 4x + 6y subject to 3x + 2y ≤ 12, x + y ≥ 4, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.
board.answer:
Draw lines 3x + 2y = 12 [passes through (4,0), (0,6)] and x + y = 4 [passes through (4,0), (0,4)].
Feasible region is bounded by corner points A(4,0), B(0,4), C(0,6).
Z(4,0) = 16; Z(0,4) = 24; Z(0,6) = 36.
Maximum Z = 36 at (0, 6).
